methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $12M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Salient Motion is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable, all operating in the robotics and manufacturing sector.

Two triangulation methods apply here. Stage-progression analysis uses the $12M total raised as a proxy for current implied value, applying a typical 2.0x multiplier for Series A progression to the next stage, yielding $24M. Peer-median analysis references four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed)—producing a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The substantial gap between methods reflects meaningful uncertainty inherent in early-stage robotics valuations. Stage-progression yields $24M; peer-median yields $1.7B. A triangulated range of $20.4M to $2.0B, with a median of $862M, reflects both approaches but should be interpreted cautiously. The peer set skews toward later-stage, higher-valuation companies (predominantly Series B); Salient Motion's earlier stage and smaller capital position suggest positioning toward the lower end of the peer range is more defensible. Key uncertainties include product maturity, commercial traction, and the sustainability of comparable company valuations in a capital-intensive sector.
